{{Quote|It's my belief that 'Rage of the Shadow Warriors' dates from the reign of Mandalore the Ultimate, when the Taungs knew they were being eclipsed. I've always thought it a poignant work—a plea that the Taungs not be forgotten by the newborn culture they knew would outlive them.|Hu Jibwe|<ref name="AncientCoruscant" />}}
'''Hu Jibwe''' was a [[Historian/Legends|scholar]] of [[Army/Legends|military]] history, employed at the [[Salmagodro Grand Academy]] during the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Era]].<ref name="AncientCoruscant" /> Some [[Time/Legends|time]] after [[15 BBY/Legends|15 BBY]],<ref name="Date">Jason Fry's "Ancient Coruscant" Blog indicates that by the time of Eschul Shaywa's [[Imperial Center Today]] article, the [[roonstone]] containing the ''Dha Werda Verda'' had already been found and housed on [[Manda/Legends|Manda]], events ''[[Star Wars Droids: The Adventures of R2-D2 and C-3PO]]'' note take place in [[15 BBY/Legends|15 BBY]].</ref> Hu spoke with ''[[Imperial Center Today]]'' contributor [[Eschul Shaywa]], and discussed the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] ''[[Dha Werda Verda]]'' chant's history and composition. A quote of Hu was later included in Shaywa's completed article, "[[A LONG TIME AGO...]]"<ref name="AncientCoruscant" />

==Behind the scenes==
Hu Jibwe was first introduced to ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] in the second installment of [[Jason Fry]]'s official [[Star Wars Blog|''Star Wars'' Blog]] series, [[Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|The Essential Guide to Warfare: Author's Cut]], entitled "Ancient Coruscant."
